QF.id: Cat III AIF Overview and Growth_11

question.text: The Indian Government (DPIIT) defines a 'start-up' (for Cat I AIF context) as a business that is:

answer.text: Not older than 10 years, with turnover not more than INR 100 crore in any financial year, and engaged in innovation/development/improvement or a scalable business model

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the DPIIT definition (p. 17), a start-up is a business that is not more than 10 years old, has turnover not more than INR 100 crore in any financial year, and is engaged in innovation, development or improvement of products/processes/services or has a scalable business model. The Trap: Thresholds such as 5 years, or any new business, or any company with fresh equity do not match the DPIIT definition. Note: All three prongs — age, turnover and the innovation/scalability criterion — must be satisfied to qualify under DPIIT.
